newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Merrill Lynch targets capital hungry Eastern Europe.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch targets capital hungry Eastern Europe.

text.p: Investment bank Merrill Lynch & Co Inc said on Wednesday it was targetting Eastern Europe this year as an emerging region hungry for investment capital.
The high-profile bank is making Russia and other former Eastern Bloc countries a high priority, especially in the area of infrastructure, as they rebuild their economies.
"The market where we will really spend a lot of energy and time on this year is in Eastern Europe," Merrill Lynch International chairman Win Smith told Reuters in an interview.
Smith was visiting Australia to review the integration of recently purchased local stockbroker McIntosh & Co.
"Infrastructure is the big deal for all of these developing countries and that will take the role of direct investment, private issuance as well as capital markets issuance," he said.
Smith said Merrill would concentrate its Eastern European efforts in Russia, Poland, Hungary and Romania.
"We will likely open at least a representative office in a couple of those countries sometime in 1997."
Previously Merrill's Eastern European clients have had their investment banking needs serviced from London, Smith said.
Smith said Merrill initially was keen to meet demand for debt and equity capital but also would offer bread and butter services like investment advice, strategic sales and capital market sales.
"I think there will be a couple (of services offered). Primarily it's going to be on the issuance side. They are heavy (consumers) of capital right now, debt and equity," he said.
Merrill Lynch has already begun to build a profile in the region, having recently been chosen as financial advisor and global coordinator to Hungarian telecoms firm Matav.
Matav, which is 67 percent owned by Deutsche Telekom AG and Ameritech Corp is mulling an initial public offering that analysts say might be as large as US$1 billion.
"We're advising a couple of Russian enterprises right now that are looking at both debt and equity issuance," Smith said.
He added telecommunications had become something of a global specialty for Merrill.

"We've developed a particular capability in telecoms. We've had a very successful track record ... and once you develop that industry expertise it's rather transferable around the world as long as you have the local supporting effort," he said.
Smith said Merrill's Eastern Europe push would not see it buy a local player, despite previously boosting its presence in several developed European countries via broker firm purchases.
"In Eastern Europe my guess is that we will probably grow indigenously at least for the time being," he said.

Smith said Merrill's other global expansion plans included building its position in the key Asian markets of China, India and Indonesia while consolidating its more than 20-year presence Latin America by offering greater debt market services.
